correctness.rationale: For the exact domain finite abelian A and char(F_q) coprime to |A|, the Fourier matrix is invertible. The dual displacement map has image size r and fibers size f. For each q-Frobenius orbit O in that image of length d, u values on its f d fiber coordinates constitute a field-defined space of q^(f d) assignments; only the zero assignment deactivates the left rank d. Right ranks activate f d rows from nonzero u values on each d-coordinate image orbit, with q^(N-r) free coordinates outside. Independent orbit choices prove the two rank enumerators, and summing kernel cardinalities gives the product count. Script verify.py exhaustively checks cyclic, nonsplit F4, and noncyclic nonlatin finite cases. Explicit no result in characteristic dividing |A|; computations are checks, not general proof.

The stated result is a genuinely additional exhaustive census of left and right multiplication ranks and zero products for arbitrary finite Alexander quandles over nonmodular finite fields, including nonsplitting coefficients and nonlatin displacement maps. No inspected prior theorem, table, or semantically matched mathematical record states or covers both rank distributions and the uniform pair count. Implicit coverage via general coordinate-product theory remains a residual priority risk, not independently ruled out.

value.rationale: These are the full distributions of a natural invariant (multiplication map rank) and the exact ordered zero-product probability for every finite Alexander quandle algebra in semisimple characteristic. The theorem handles all nonlatin automorphisms and non-splitting finite fields, resolves the left/right rank asymmetry, and reduces the arithmetic to the displacement subgroup and its Frobenius orbits. It is a meaningful complete classification rather than one arbitrary table or a claim of the known Fourier identity.
